effective_date_basis: The earliest of: a superseding order, lapse or repeal of the order's statutory authority, an express repeal by codification, the order's own terms, X1-E3.
ending_pattern: Candidate end: the Canal Zone ceased on October 1, 1979 (event X1-E3), but most orders ended earlier: by supersession; by lapse or repeal of the specific statutory authority (the exemplar EO 5888 rests on the Canal Zone liquor provision added to the National Prohibition Act in 1932 (47 Stat. 579; 27 U.S.C. 63), which was repealed on June 19, 1934 (48 Stat. 1116, s.3); that Act also gave the President new liquor-rule authority for the Canal Zone, so a successor order may exist and must be checked); or on their own terms. A codification (the Canal Zone Code) ends an order only where the Code or its enacting act expressly repeals or replaces it; otherwise it is a lead. The earliest end controls.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Functions continued by the Panama Canal Commission after 1979 are savings, not ends.

exemplar.wpa_summary: Canal Zone regulations governing liquor transportation prescribed. M 440; XXVI PCRec 10.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
One-person appointments (spent on issue rather than swept).

The 30-month treaty transition (Panama Canal Treaty art. XI; Panama Canal Act of 1979): some U.S. jurisdiction and transitional courts continued past Oct. 1, 1979 (to about March 31, 1982), so orders on courts, police or criminal law may have a later end.
Panama Railroad / Panama Canal Company corporate matters resting on corporate statutes.
